correction.text: Egypt as a Persian possession: the page describes the satrapy only as Egypt and gives no borders

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; Cliopatria's Twenty-sixth Dynasty row runs on to -501 and its Achaemenid rows are not Egypt-specific). The battle page: "Egypt became a possession of Persia, and Cambyses its Pharaoh." The 27th page: the satrapy was joined with Cyprus and Phoenicia to form "the sixth satrapy", which is not drawn here. Cambyses made peace with the Libyans, so the Libyan coast is not added. No infobox area.

correction.text: Egypt without the western Delta around Sais, where Inaros II ruled; the Persians kept Memphis

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for the revolt of Inaros II: he held Libyans from Mareia and the Delta around Sais; part of the Persian army held the Memphis citadel, the White Castle (Inaros II page; the Egypt (satrapy) page says Persian rule "remained in place in Memphis"). The 27th page instead says Inaros took Memphis; the two pages disagree and Memphis is drawn Persian. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Alexandria radius (Mareia) added to the subtracted rebel land, matching the revolt-of-inaros-ii keyframe.

correction.text: Egypt again wholly Persian after Megabyzus defeated Inaros in 454

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 27th page says Megabyzus "finally defeated" Inaros and his Athenian allies in 454. From 405 Amyrtaeus held Memphis (28th page); the pages give no extent for the last year of the dynasty, so the shape is kept to 404. No infobox area.

region.text: Egypt, the whole Nile Valley and Delta

ledger.note: 525: Cambyses II wins Egypt at Pelusium and the Twenty-seventh Dynasty begins. The 27th page dates the battle to May 525 ("defeated by [Cambyses II] at the Battle of Pelusium in the eastern Nile Delta in May of 525"); the battle page says Cambyses "took Memphis, and captured King Psammetichus III" and "Egypt became a possession of Persia, and Cambyses its Pharaoh."

525: Egypt is held by the Persian kings as the First Egyptian Satrapy (525-404). The scope of this group draws the Persian periods as occupations, hatched over Egypt's own colour; the pages call it a possession of Persia and a satrapy, so the status is the researcher's reading. Owner-side record; achaemenid-empire (me-05) holds the occupier-side event.

region.text: the Nile Delta around Sais and the Libyan coast at Mareia

ledger.note: 460: Inaros II raises the western Delta. The Inaros II page says "In 460 BC, he revolted against the Persians" and "held a kingship over the Libyans from Mareia (above Pharos) and the part of the Nile Delta around Sais"; the 27th page says the Athenians substantially assisted him. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Alexandria radius (stand-in for Mareia) added so the region matches its text and the Inaros dossier's found region.

460: the Persian army, led by the satrap Achaemenes, is defeated and the Persians fall back on the Memphis citadel. The Inaros II page says Achaemenes was "defeated and killed at Papremis" and the White Castle at Memphis "could not be dislodged"; the 27th page says Inaros took Memphis.

454: Megabyzus ends the revolt. The 27th page says he "finally defeated" Inaros and his Athenian allies in 454; the Athenians, besieged on the island of Prosopitis for eighteen months, were beaten (Inaros II page: "the Athenians were finally defeated in 454 BC by the Persian army").

region.text: the Nile Delta around Sais and the Libyan coast at Mareia

ledger.note: 454: the western Delta returns to Persian rule after Inaros is defeated and taken to Susa. [Reviewer me-03-x, 2026-10-19] Alexandria radius (Mareia) added to mirror the loss of 460.

405: Amyrtaeus expels the Persians from Memphis. The 28th page says he "succeeded in expelling the Persians from Memphis in 405 BC" with Cretan mercenaries (27th page: the rebellion may date from 411).
404: the Persian war for Egypt ends in an Egyptian success; Amyrtaeus proclaims himself Pharaoh after Darius II's death.

region.text: Egypt, the whole Nile Valley and Delta

ledger.note: 404: Egypt breaks away from Persia. The infobox of the 28th page gives "End of Satrapy: 404 BC"; the Egypt (satrapy) page says Egypt "detached from Persian administration". The 27th page notes Artaxerxes II was still recognised as pharaoh in parts of Egypt as late as 401; no region is given, so the whole valley is drawn lost in 404.
404: Persian rule over Egypt ends (infobox 404; the body text says Amyrtaeus expelled the Persians in 405 and was crowned the next year). Owner-side record of the occupier's loss.
404: the Twenty-seventh Dynasty ends with the rebellion of Amyrtaeus. The infobox says Disestablished 404 BC.

wars.name: Battle of Pelusium (525 BC)
wars.outcome: Persian victory: Cambyses II took Memphis, captured Psamtik III and became pharaoh; the Libyans made a truce.

wars.outcome: A native prince rebelled in late 522 or early 521 and Darius reportedly ended the revolt; no territory is described.

wars.name: Revolt of Amyrtaeus
wars.outcome: Egyptian victory: the Persians were expelled from Memphis in 405 and Amyrtaeus declared himself pharaoh in 404.

notes:
Modelling choice: Cliopatria has no Egyptian row for 525-404 (its Twenty-sixth Dynasty row runs on to -501 with a Levantine reach, reviewed by me-03-c), and the group scope asks for the Persian periods as occupations. This dossier therefore draws Egypt as a land (family egypt) under Persian pharaohs, with occupation_start/end naming achaemenid-empire; the me-05 Achaemenid dossier should carry the reverse events and should not also draw Egypt as plain Achaemenid territory in 525-404 and 343-332, or the two will overlap. The pages themselves call it a satrapy and a possession of Persia, so the occupation label is a choice of the scope, not of the pages.

Disagreements: the 27th page says Inaros took Memphis, the Egypt (satrapy) and Inaros II pages say the Persians held the White Castle; the dynasty's end is 404 (infobox) or 405/404 (text); Aryandes is deposed twice by two accounts. The line that Egypt, Cyprus and Phoenicia formed 'the sixth satrapy' came back from the fetch of the 27th page; Herodotus' sixth satrapy is Egypt with Libya and Cyrene, so that sentence should be rechecked by a reviewer. The pages name no capital, no area and no border, and say nothing about Libya, Cyrenaica or Nubia as parts of the satrapy (Herodotus' satrapy list, which would add them, was not opened). Petubastis III (522/521-520), Psamtik IV (480) and Khababash (see the 31st dossier) are short rebel pharaohs written as wars, not dossiers; the revolt of Inaros II (6 years, land held) is a rebel dossier.
